items.title: Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2022
items.q: The interviewee discusses Dave Brubeck's music and the cultural context of the era, while the interviewer mentions Jackson Pollock as a social/cultural parallel. The interviewee does not mention Pollock or express a personal connection.

ctx.x: Right they’re in a diner and they have a juke box like that and they start playing “Take Five” and they’re going like, and you can see their ears start to turn pink and it’s like their brains are like — and they end up being in color. And they’re going, “What’s wrong with me, what’s going on” you know it’s like, I wish I could talk to that director someday because there it is. It’s like Dave thought out of the box. It’s a beat. It’s not 4/4, it’s 5/4. I think one of the reasons “Take Five” was popular is the sort…

Yeah and I guess socially the implication is like okay we’re going from a drab world to the world’s opening up and the colors are opening and Jackson Pollock’s throwing paint. And you know the whole thing happened in that time period that really revolutionized the future, and even the acceptance of the Beatles and all that. There was a lot of groundwork that was laid.

Then Dave in his older years would say, “When I look back at it I guess in a way I was kind of a pioneer of world music.” You know the stuff that came back from that tour that made it into jazz. And of course he was following the advice of Milhaud saying the same thing about when you travel open your ears, incorporate music you hear in other countries into what you’re doing and then you’ll be an innovator helping your art form grow.
